references.text: Jesus quotes directly from Isaiah 53:12: "He was counted among transgressors" (Καὶ μετὰ ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη). This prophecy from the suffering servant song concerns the Messiah who bears the sins of many and is placed among lawbreakers—something that was literally fulfilled when Jesus was crucified between two criminals.
Jesus was arrested as a criminal when they came with swords and clubs, which concretely fulfilled the prophecy that he would be "counted among lawbreakers" (Luke 22:52-53).
Mark quotes the same prophecy from Isaiah 53:12 in connection with Jesus being crucified between two thieves: "He was counted among transgressors" (Mark 15:27-28).
The literal fulfillment of the prophecy occurred when Jesus was crucified together with two criminals at Golgotha (Luke 23:32-33).

The entire chapter of Isaiah 53 concerns the suffering servant who was despised, rejected, and wounded for our transgressions. Isaiah 53:3-5 provides the broader context for the prophecy Jesus quotes about being counted among lawless ones.

After the resurrection, Jesus explained that everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to be fulfilled (Luke 24:44). This corresponds to the words in 22:37 that "what is written must be fulfilled" (δεῖ τελεσθῆναι).

Philip explains to the Ethiopian eunuch the text from Isaiah 53:7-8 and shows that this refers to Jesus (Acts 8:32-33). This confirms that the early church understood Isaiah 53 as a messianic prophecy fulfilled in Jesus.

Peter applies Isaiah 53 directly to Jesus, including that "he who bore our sins in his body on the tree" (1 Peter 2:22-24). This shows the broader apostolic understanding that the suffering servant prophecy was fulfilled in Christ.
